capitals.note: Varman page: the older city 'is presumed' Pragjyotishpura on 'the south-eastern slope of the Narakasur hill near Dispur'; the page gives no start year.

capitals.note: 'The capital was moved at least once, the last time by Sthitavarman (566-590)'; the new capital was 'possibly some location in Guwahati', with no archaeological support. Bhaskaravarman's grants were issued from camps, among them Karnasuvarna.

capitals.note: Mlechchha page: 'from their capital at Harruppesvar in present-day Tezpur'; the Kamarupa page gives Hadapeshvara as the first Pala capital.

capitals.name: Durjaya (North Guwahati)
capitals.note: 'Under Ratna Pala (r. 920-960), it moved to Durjaya, near Guwahati.'

capitals.name: Kamarupanagara (North Guwahati)
capitals.note: 'Dharma Pala made Kamarupanagara (North Guwahati) his capital' (1035-1060); the pages name no capital for Timgyadeva or Vaidyadeva, so the span runs to the end by default.

rulers.name: Pushyavarman
rulers.note: Varman dynasty; the king lists on the Kamarupa and Varman pages have gaps (no kings between 398 and 422, 446 and 470, 494 and 518, 542 and 566).

rulers.name: Susthitavarman
rulers.note: The Kamarupa page gives 590-600 with Suprathisthitavarman reigning briefly c. 595-600.

rulers.name: Salastambha
rulers.note: Mlechchha dynasty; the Mlechchha page gives 650-670. The Mlechchha list has gaps between 670 and 725, 745 and 815, and 880 and 890.

rulers.name: Brahma Pala
rulers.note: Pala (Bhauma) dynasty; 'elected as king by the ruling chieftains'.

rulers.name: Dharma Pala
rulers.note: The page lists no king for 1060-1075.

rulers.name: Jaya Pala
rulers.note: 'The last known ruler of this line'.

rulers.name: Timgyadeva
rulers.title: governor for the Pala king of Gauda
rulers.note: The Kamarupa page says he 'ruled western Kamarupa independently for some time'; the Pala page makes him Ramapala's governor who 'had earlier broken from Pala control'.

rulers.name: Vaidyadeva
rulers.note: Minister of Kumarapala; 'declared independence within four years of his rule'.

correction.text: unchanged shape, holding 1072-1099 only (a change of years)

correction.text: unchanged shape, holding 1126-1140 (a change of years)

'Vaidyadeva, who ruled between 1126 and 1140' declared independence 'within four years of his rule'; the infobox on the Kamarupa page gives 'disestablished 1140', two years after Cliopatria's last year. The shape holds 1126-1140 (a change of years).

region.text: around present-day Guwahati

ledger.note: 350: Pushyavarman founds the Varman dynasty of Kamarupa near Guwahati. 'Pushyavarman (350-374) established the Varman Dynasty'; infobox 'established 350'; 'Kamarupa began as a subordinate but sovereign ally of the Gupta Empire' around present-day Guwahati in the 4th century. Overlap (repair pass, 2026-10-19): the 150 km Guwahati core shares 87 cells (about 22,000 km2) with Cliopatria's Gupta Empire shape of 347, which the gupta-empire dossier releases only in 353 (its /ledger 'loss' of Kamarupa), so both dossiers draw those cells in 350-352; the page side is right (infobox 'established 350'), so the gupta-empire loss should move to 350 or its 347 gain should leave the Guwahati core (routed to sa-02). The 'subordinate but sovereign ally' relation is not recorded as a vassal pair here: the page calls Kamarupa sovereign, gives no end for the alliance, and the gupta-empire dossier draws Kamarupa as a plain gain (347) and loss (353), not a vassal.

region.text: the Brahmaputra valley and the Meghalaya edge shared by the Gupta 347 and Kamarupa 353 shapes

ledger.note: 353: Kamarupa takes the Brahmaputra valley edge of the Gupta shape. Cliopatria draws the transfer; the Kamarupa page has only 'Samudragupta's Allahabad pillar inscription calls the kings of Kamarupa and Davaka frontier rulers', i.e. tributary frontier kings rather than land lost. The Gupta dossier records the matching loss at 353.

region.text: the rest of the 353 shape beyond the Gupta cells: the upper Brahmaputra valley and the hills

ledger.note: 353: the Kamarupa shape of Cliopatria stands in full. The page names only the core around Guwahati and the traditional bounds (Karatoya to Sadiya); the rest of the 353 shape (Meghalaya, Arunachal, Nagaland, Bhutan) rests on Cliopatria alone.

region.text: Davaka in the Kapili river valley, present-day Nagaon district

ledger.note: c. 422: Kalyanavarman occupies Davaka. 'Kalyanavarman (422-446) occupied Davaka'; Davaka lay 'in the Kapili river valley in present-day Nagaon district' and is not mentioned as independent after the 5th century. The year is the start of his reign; Cliopatria's 353 shape already contains these cells.

region.text: Chandrapuri visaya, 'identified with the Sylhet Division'

ledger.note: 518-542: Bhutivarman extends Kamarupa to the Sylhet Division. 'Per the Nidhanpur inscription, expansion included Chandrapuri visaya, which is identified with the Sylhet Division'; the page gives the reign (518-542) but no year for the gain and names no former owner.
566-590: Sthitavarman moves the capital. 'The capital was moved at least once, the last time by Sthitavarman (566-590)'; the new seat was 'possibly some location in Guwahati'.

region.text: Karnasuvarna, Shashanka's capital 'in present day India' (Murshidabad)

ledger.note: c. 637: Bhaskaravarman takes Karnasuvarna after Shashanka's death. 'After the death of Shasanka the capital city Karnasuvarna passed in to the hands of Bhaskaravarman'; 'Gauda was soon divided amongst Harsha and Bhaskaravarman of Kamarupa'. Shashanka's infobox gives 636 as his death; the page does not say 'soon' in years, and Harsha took the rest of Gauda. Repair pass (2026-10-19), Gauda Kingdom page opened: 'Gauda was soon divided amongst Harshavardhana and Bhaskarvarmana of Kamarupa, the latter even managing to conquer Karnasuvarna'; its infobox dates read 'c. 4th century AD (pre-Gupta) 554-636' (the extract did not show the field labels) and it puts Shashanka's rule 'approximately between 593 and 636', while Cliopatria's Gauda Kingdom row is only 602-611. The counterpart stays gauda-kingdom: the sa-03 gauda-kingdom dossier has to run to 636/637 for this gain to be matched (otherwise the counterpart is harsha-s-empire or nobody).

655: Salastambha ends the Varman line and founds the Mlechchha dynasty. 'The kingdom passed into the hands of Salasthambha (r. 655-670)' after Bhaskaravarman died without an heir; the Varman page says the dynasty 'was overthrown by Salastambha, a man of Mleccha or non-Aryan origin' and gives 655; the Mlechchha page's infobox says 650. Same state, same colour.
655: the capital moves to Haruppeswara. The Mlechchha dynasty ruled 'from their capital at Harruppesvar in present-day Tezpur'.

region.text: Bhutan and the hill edge that the 656 shape no longer holds, outside the Tibetan Empire shape (130 cells, 90.2-95.3 E, 25.2-28.1 N)

ledger.note: 656: the hills and Bhutan leave the Kamarupa shape. Cliopatria's 656 shape lacks 163 cells of the 655 shape (Bhutan, part of Arunachal Pradesh); 130 of them lie in no state's shape and are recorded here as lost to nobody (the other 33 lie in the Tibetan Empire shape of 656: see the next event). The Mlechchha page says nothing of the loss.

region.text: the north edge (91.6-94.0 E, 27.5-28.2 N), 33 cells, that the 656 shape no longer holds and that lie inside Cliopatria's Tibetan Empire shape of 656

ledger.note: 656: 33 cells (about 8,300 km2) of the Kamarupa shape's northern edge pass to the Tibetan Empire shape. Cliopatria's 656 Kamarupa shape lacks 163 cells of its 655 shape, 33 of which lie in its Tibetan Empire shape of 656 (none in its 655 shape). The Tibetan Empire page (opened 2026-10-19) places no conquest in Bhutan, Arunachal or Assam in the 650s ('In 645, Songtsen Gampo overran the kingdom of Zhangzhung'; the Tuyuhun fall in 663), mentions Bhutan only as the place of Mutik Tsenpo's exile, and has the empire reach 'the Himalayas and Bengal' only 'in the opening years of the 9th century'; the transfer is Cliopatria's drawing, not a page event. The tibetan-empire dossier (ea-04) should mirror the gain or say it does not.

region.text: Sylhet (Chandrapuri visaya) and Karnasuvarna

ledger.note: 656: Sylhet and Karnasuvarna are not in Cliopatria's 656 shape. Neither the Mlechchha nor the Kamarupa page says that Bhaskaravarman's Karnasuvarna or Bhutivarman's Sylhet was lost; the Mlechchha page says only that the kingdom 'broke up' after Harshavarman.

region.text: north Bengal and the lower Brahmaputra west of the 655 shape

ledger.note: 656: north Bengal enters the Kamarupa shape. Cliopatria's 656 shape holds 59 cells (88.3-95.2 E, 25.2-27.3 N) that the 655 shape lacks and that no neighbouring Cliopatria shape held; the pages date nothing here.

region.text: the north Bengal and Rangpur land of the 656 shape

ledger.note: 751: the north Bengal land leaves Kamarupa. Cliopatria's 751 shape is 70 cells smaller than the 656 shape (8 of them in its Pala Empire shape); the Mlechchha page says only 'After Harshavarman's death, the empire broke up, leaving a small country in Northern Bengal known as Kamarupa' (Harshavarman reigned 725-745).

region.text: Pragjyotisha (present-day Assam), whose king 'submitted without giving a fight'

ledger.note: c. 810: the king of Pragjyotisha submits to Devapala. 'His expeditions resulted in the invasion of Pragjyotisha (present-day Assam) where the king submitted without giving a fight'; 'Pragjyotisa or Assam accepted the suzerainty of Devapala'; 'the king of Assam was either Pralambha or Harjara'. The page dates Devapala's reign (810-c. 850 Majumdar; 812-850 Sircar), not the submission, so 810 is the reign's start (bridged, confidence 1); the land is the drawn Kamarupa shape, which the page calls Pragjyotisha. Kamarupa is the vassal and pala-empire the suzerain: the pala-empire dossier (sa-03) should hold the mirror vassal_start with counterpart kamarupa-kingdom. The Kamarupa page does not mention the submission; /wars/4 keeps the campaign, with no contested zone because the king did not fight.

region.text: Assam, which 'Narayanapala lost control of'

ledger.note: c. 860: Kamarupa slips out of Pala suzerainty. 'Narayanapala lost control of Assam and Orissa'; 'Encouraged by the Pala decline, the King Harjara of Assam assumed imperial titles.' Narayanapala reigned 854-908 (Majumdar) or 860-917 (Sircar) and the page gives no year for the loss, so 860 is Sircar's accession and the year of Cliopatria's 860 shape (bridged, confidence 1). The pages disagree on timing: the dossier's ruler list (Mlechchha page) dates Harjaravarman 815-832, before Narayanapala, so the 'imperial titles' may precede 854. Mirror: pala-empire vassal_end with counterpart kamarupa-kingdom. The Kamarupa pages record no Pala overlord at any time.

900: Brahma Pala founds the Pala (Bhauma) line. 'Brahma Pala (r. 900-920), was elected as king by the ruling chieftains' after Tyagasimha (890-900) (Kamarupa page; the Pala (Kamarupa) page says only that the first ruler 'was elected'); the Pala page's infobox: 'Established: 900 CE'. Same state, same colour.
900: the Pala kings rule from Hadapeshvara (Harruppeshvar near Tezpur). 'The original capital was Hadapeshvara'; the Pala page names Harruppeshvar (Tezpur).
c. 920: Ratna Pala moves the capital to Durjaya. 'Under Ratna Pala (r. 920-960), it moved to Durjaya, near Guwahati.'

region.text: Arunachal Pradesh and the Himalayan edge held by the Tibetans in 959

ledger.note: 960: the traditional Kamarupa extent is drawn in the Arunachal hills. Cliopatria's 960 shape adds 190 cells that lie in its last Tibetan Empire shape (849); the Kamarupa page's only extents are 'Kamarupa at its height covered the entire Brahmaputra Valley, parts of North Bengal, Bhutan' and the traditional bounds, undated. Reviewer (sa-02-e, 2026-10-19): the Tibetan Empire row ends in 849, so it cannot be the counterpart in 960; 75 of the 190 cells lie in Cliopatria's Tibetans shape of 959 (and none in its 960 shape), so this gain is those 75 cells from tibetans and the other 115 join the 'nobody' gain below.

region.text: Bhutan, north Bengal, Rangpur, Sikkim and the Bihar edge added in 960

ledger.note: 960: Bhutan, north Bengal and Sikkim join the Kamarupa shape. The Pala dynasty list has Indra Pala in 960, whose page gives no war ('addicted more to study than to war'), so the 345 added cells outside the Tibetan shape are Cliopatria's reading of the traditional boundary ('Kanchenjanga in the north', Karatoya in the west). Reviewer (sa-02-e): the region is now everything added in 960 outside the Tibetans shape of 959 (460 cells; 115 of them were in the Tibetan Empire shape of 849).
1035: Dharma Pala makes Kamarupanagara (North Guwahati) the capital. 'Dharma Pala made Kamarupanagara (North Guwahati) his capital' (reign 1035-1060).

region.text: north Bengal and the Goalpara edge in the Pala Empire shape of 1056

ledger.note: 1056: the west of the Kamarupa shape falls to the Pala shape. Cliopatria's 1056 shape drops 247 cells in the west (95 of them in its Pala Empire shape of 1056). The Pala (Kamarupa) page, reign of Dharma Pala (1035-1060), mentions no war; the Pala Empire page dates nothing in Kamarupa before Ramapala.

region.text: the Himalayan edge, Sikkim, Nepal and Bhutan foothills dropped in 1056

ledger.note: 1056: the rest of the dropped west is stateless in Cliopatria. 152 of the 247 cells dropped in 1056 lie in no neighbour's shape.

region.text: the Patkai hills and the upper Brahmaputra east of the 1055 shape

ledger.note: 1056: the east grows into the Patkai hills. Cliopatria's 1056 shape adds 108 cells (40 in Myanmar, 14 in its Tibetan shape); no page on the Pala (Kamarupa) line mentions the east.

region.text: the Garo Hills and Mymensingh side

ledger.note: 1072: the south-west leaves the Kamarupa shape for the Sena shape (32 cells at 90.8-92.4 E, 25.3-26.0 N). The Sena dynasty begins in Cliopatria in 1072; no page dates the transfer.

region.text: western Kamarupa: Kamarupanagara and the lower Brahmaputra

ledger.note: 1100: Ramapala ends the Pala line and takes western Kamarupa. 'The Pala dynasty came to an end when Kamarupa was invaded by the Gaur king Ramapala'; infobox 'Disestablished: 1100'; the Kamarupa page: 'its western territories were conquered by Ramapala'. The invasion year is not on any page (the Ramapala page: 'brought Kamarupa and Rarh under his control', reign 1077-1130); 1100 is the end of Jaya Pala's reign, and 'Timgyadeva was made the governor of Kamarupa who ruled between 1110 and 1126'.

region.text: western Kamarupa, ruled by Vaidyadeva

ledger.note: 1126: Vaidyadeva takes western Kamarupa back. 'Vaidyadeva, who ruled between 1126 and 1140'; he 'declared independence within four years of his rule, after Kumarapala's death' and 'practically created a separate kingdom' (Pala Empire page, which dates Kumarapala 1126-1128 by Sircar and 1130-1140 by Majumdar).

region.text: the last Kamarupa shape, which splits among the Lunar dynasty, the Sylhet chiefs and later Kamata, Ahom, Chutia and Kachari states

ledger.note: 1140: the Kamarupa kingdom ends. Infobox 'Disestablished 1140' (Vaidyadeva reigned 1126-1140); 'The historical kingdom disappeared by the 12th century' and 'is believed to have broken up entirely by the 13th century', after which Sandhya founded Kamata (c. 1250-1270) and the Ahom, Chutia, Kachari and Baro-Bhuyan states rose. Cliopatria's last year is 1138.

wars.name: Yasodharman's attack on Kamarupa
wars.outcome: The page calls it 'the first major assault from the west' and says the effect is unclear; no land is named.

wars.name: Later Gupta and Gauda attacks on Kamarupa
wars.outcome: Susthitavarman 'came under the attack of Mahasenagupta of East Malwa' (Kamarupa page) and 'was defeated by Mahasengupta on the bank of Lauhitya' (Varman page, 590-595); the Gauda army 'carried out attacks against the Varman King Susthitavarman' between about 595 and 600, took princes who 'were brought back to Gauda as prisoners but released shortly thereafter' and 'returned to their kingdom as feudatories under Shashanka'. No land changes hands.
wars.note: Earlier, Sthitavarman (566-590) 'enjoyed victories over the Gauda Kingdom of Karnasuvarna' (Kamarupa page). The pages disagree on who beat Susthitavarman: Mahasenagupta or Gauda.

wars.name: Bhaskaravarman and Harsha against Shashanka's Gauda
wars.outcome: Bhaskaravarman allied with Harshavardhana (taken c. 606) against Gauda; after Shashanka's death 'Gauda was soon divided amongst Harsha and Bhaskaravarman', who 'even managing to conquer Karnasuvarna'.
wars.note: No campaign or battle is dated on the pages; the span runs from the alliance (Kamarupa page: c. 606) to Shashanka's death (636). No contest events are written.

wars.name: Kamarupa-Kannauj war of Harshavarman and Yasovarman
wars.outcome: Yasovarman of Kannauj 'competed with him for control of Northern India'; 'Harshavarman was defeated and killed'; the Gaudavadha of Vakapati celebrated the victory without naming the king. After his death 'the empire broke up'.
wars.note: The page gives no year for the battle and calls it the Battle of Bihar; Harshavarman's dates (725-745) are from the Ratnapala grants. It also says Kamarupa kings were 'said to hold Gauda, Odra, Kaling, Koshala' in the first quarter of the 8th century and that 'Historians are unsure whether Harshavarman or his predecessor conquered Gauda'; this claim is not drawn.

wars.name: Pala invasion of Pragjyotisha under Devapala
wars.outcome: 'the invasion of Pragjyotisha (present-day Assam) where the king submitted without giving a fight'; 'Pragjyotisa or Assam accepted the suzerainty of Devapala'; 'it has been inferred that the king of Assam was either Pralambha or Harjara'.
wars.note: Span is Devapala's reign (Majumdar 810-850; Sircar 812-850); the page gives no year for the invasion. The vassal relation is recorded in the ledger (vassal_start 810, vassal_end 860, counterpart pala-empire); the pala-empire dossier (sa-03) should hold the mirror. The Kamarupa page does not mention the invasion.

wars.name: Ramapala's conquest of Kamarupa
wars.outcome: 'The Pala dynasty came to an end when Kamarupa was invaded by the Gaur king Ramapala'; 'Timgyadeva was made the governor of Kamarupa who ruled between 1110 and 1126'; Ramapala 'could not keep control for long'.
wars.note: The years are the end of the Pala line (1100) and the start of Timgyadeva's governorship (1110); the Ramapala page gives no year for the conquest (reign 1077-1130).

wars.name: Vaidyadeva's revolt in Kamarupa
wars.outcome: 'a rebellion broke out in Kamarupa' in Kumarapala's reign, 'crushed by Vaidyadeva, minister of Kumarapala'; 'after Kumarapala's death, Vaidyadeva practically created a separate kingdom'.
wars.note: The Pala (Kamarupa) page: Vaidyadeva (1126-1140) 'declared independence within four years of his rule'. The two pages differ on whether the rebellion was crushed first.

certainty.note: No page gives a surveyed or treaty boundary for Kamarupa. Only the 'traditional boundary' (Karatoya in the west, Sadiya in the east, between the Dhaka and Mymensingh districts in the south, 'Kanchenjanga in the north') is named, undated; every frontier stays soft.

notes: Page budget up to 9 pages, all used (nine distinct pages, the Kamarupa page read twice). THE ROW: Cliopatria keeps one row for 785 years; the Kamarupa page treats it as one kingdom ('Kamarupa prevailed from 350 to 1140 CE') under three dynasties (Varman 350-655, Mlechchha or Salastambha 655-900, Pala or Bhauma 900-1100) plus a fragmented tail, so it is one dossier with two rename events (655 and 900); a split would be possible but no page treats the dynasties as separate states. SHAPES: no page gives an area or dates an extent for any year, so 12 of the 13 shapes are 'unverified: page budget'. The jumps at 656 (hills lost, north Bengal gained), 960 (x2.5, the traditional extent from Karatoya to Sadiya to Kanchenjanga, 190 of the added cells inside the last Tibetan Empire shape), 1056 (west dropped, east and Myanmar added) and 1072 are Cliopatria's and none of the nine pages explains them; they are recorded at confidence 1. A gap-filler should open 'Davaka', 'Kamarupa' on Seshat and the Tibetan Empire and Sena pages. DISAGREEMENTS: the Mlechchha page begins the line in 650 and the Kamarupa page in 655; Susthitavarman 590-595 (Varman page) or 590-600 (Kamarupa page); who beat him (Mahasenagupta or Gauda); Timgyadeva 'independent' (Kamarupa page) or Ramapala's governor (Pala page); the end 1140 (infobox) against 'the 12th century' and 'the 13th century' (text); the Mlechchha page puts Harshavarman 725-745 yet his defeat by Yasovarman is placed in the Gaudavadha tradition. NOT DRAWN: the Mlechchha page's claim that Harshavarman held 'much of eastern India' and that Kamarupa kings were 'said to hold Gauda, Odra, Kaling, Koshala' is not drawn as territory (undated, 'historians are unsure'); a gap-filler may add it as a soft claim. VASSALAGE OWNED BY OTHERS: Kamarupa as a frontier tributary of the Guptas (Allahabad pillar) belongs to the gupta-empire dossier (its 353 loss is matched here); Devapala's suzerainty over Pragjyotisha (c. 810-850) and Narayanapala's loss of Assam are now recorded here as vassal_start 810 and vassal_end 860 (counterpart pala-empire, confidence 1); the pala-empire dossier should hold the mirror with counterpart 'kamarupa-kingdom'. STATES NEEDING DOSSIERS: davaka (a Kapili-valley kingdom, 4th-5th century), kamata-kingdom (c. 1250), ahom-kingdom (1228), chutia-kingdom, kachari-kingdom, and the Lunar dynasty and Sylhet chiefs of the 12th century. GAZETTEER: 'Karnasuvarna', 'Nagaon', 'Sadiya', 'Chandrapuri' and the Karatoya river are absent; the dossier uses a 50 km circle at 24.07 N 88.25 E and a 60 km circle at 26.35 N 92.68 E, and the Guwahati place for the core and western Kamarupa (120-150 km). Kapili valley and Dikkaravasini were not used. REPAIR PASS 2026-10-19 (after review): (1) vassal_start 810 / vassal_end 860 with pala-empire added (Pala Empire page reopened; the years are bridged from the reign dates, the pages disagree on whether Harjara's imperial titles fall before Narayanapala); (2) the 656 loss split into 33 cells to tibetan-empire and 130 to nobody (Tibetan Empire page opened: silent, so confidence 1, Cliopatria's drawing); (3) /ledger/0 and the 350 keyframe now say that the Guwahati core overlaps the Gupta 347 shape by 87 cells in 350-352 and that gupta-empire should release them in 350; the optional vassal pair with gupta-empire was NOT added (the page says 'sovereign ally', gives no end, and the Gupta dossier has no vassal event for Kamarupa); (4) /ledger/6 keeps gauda-kingdom as counterpart and records that the Gauda Kingdom page runs the state to 636 (infobox dates '554-636', labels not shown) against Cliopatria's 602-611, so the sa-03 dossier must run to 636/637.
